description: Every metric, freshness rule, regime and alert rule the plugin computes, defined once. Tools, the dashboard tab and the commentary skill read these definitions; code in hl_desk/ implements them and tests in tests/ check each one against independently calculated values.

sources.hyperliquid_docs: See docs/ENDPOINTS.md for every endpoint and the doc link that confirms it.
sources.hl_deck: The author's terminal Flow Deck, hl_deck.py (a private tool, not distributed; the version of 2026-10-09, 547 lines). Regime, card and latch definitions marked source=hl_deck are ported from it; the code is not copied. Line numbers refer to that file.
sources.handoff: Definitions marked source=handoff come from Handoff 1 (burst alert, wallet shares, depth bands). Definitions marked source=plugin are this plugin's own choices, documented here because neither the docs nor hl_deck define them.

conventions.time: Source times are Hyperliquid's millisecond timestamps (the 'time' field). Local receive times are the collector's monotonic clock in nanoseconds. Receipt-progress ages use the monotonic clock. Source recency compares the local wall clock with source time through the clock relationship in freshness.clock_relationship, whose uncertainty must be known; otherwise nothing source-timestamped is fresh.
conventions.notional: USD notional = px * sz (docs notation: 'Ntl ... USD amount, Px * Sz'). Sizes are in units of the coin (docs notation: 'Sz ... In units of coin, i.e. base currency').
conventions.side: Trade side follows the docs: 'B = Bid = Buy, A = Ask = Short. Side is aggressing side for trades.' side=B means the buyer was the aggressor (taker); side=A means the seller was. users = [buyer, seller].
conventions.aggressor_address: The taker of a trade is users[0] when side=B and users[1] when side=A.
conventions.trade_identity: A trade is identified by (coin, time, tid), following the docs: 'For a globally unique trade id, use (block_time, coin, tid)'. The docs don't say that WsTrade.time is the block time; this plugin assumes it is. A trade whose identity was already seen is a duplicate and is counted once.
conventions.execution_set: The flow metric's execution set for a market: every unique trade with time strictly after the current coverage segment's start, up to the trades watermark. The wallets panel, the Flow Deck and burst alerts all use this same set.
conventions.coverage_segment: A segment starts when the collector subscribes to a market's trades on a connection: its start is the latest trade time in the first trades message on that connection (that message is treated as the subscription snapshot, because the docs don't say whether it holds every recent trade). It ends at the trades watermark when the connection closes, restarts or is forced to reconnect. Nothing counts trades across two segments; the time between them is a gap.
conventions.gap: A gap is the interval between one segment's last trades watermark and the next segment's start. Every disconnect, restart and forced reconnect creates one. Gaps are listed per market in hl_status.
conventions.level_count: Each book level carries n, shown as 'API count'. Hyperliquid's docs describe n two ways: '// number of levels' (info endpoint l2Book example) and '// number of orders' (websocket WsLevel). Levels are aggregated, so a level is never an individual order.
conventions.null_rule: Missing, partial, stale, unverified or warming-up values are null with a reason, never zero. A computed zero (for example no aggressive selling in a complete, fresh window) is a real zero.
conventions.data_check: Before release, the data check verifies public trade semantics (aggressor side, identity, users order, notional) for every flow number.

statuses.fresh: Both checks pass: the field's progress signal advanced within its receipt-age limit (monotonic clock), and its source timestamp is within its source-age limit under the clock relationship's known uncertainty.
statuses.delayed: The feed is advancing, but its source timestamp is older than the source-age limit by more than the clock uncertainty: a backlog or a delayed source. Values are null.
statuses.stale: The field has a progress signal that should keep advancing (l2Book pushes on a cadence), and it hasn't within its receipt-age limit.
statuses.unverified: Freshness can't be established: no verified progress signal (bbo always; trades after their receipt-age limit with no new trade), no source timestamp (activeAssetCtx always), an unknown clock uncertainty, or a source age within the clock uncertainty of its limit.
statuses.warming_up: Nothing has been received for this field on the current connection yet, or a window doesn't yet have enough coverage.
statuses.missing: Nothing has ever been received for this field.

freshness.rechecked: The state owner rebuilds every snapshot once per second whether or not a message arrived, so a field turns stale or unverified on time even when the socket is silent. A connected socket, a pong or a websocket ping never makes data fresh.

l2Book.progress_signal: WsBook.time strictly greater than the previous push's time on the same subscription. The docs: 'Snapshot feed, pushed on each block that is at least 0.5 since last push' (no unit given; this plugin reads it as seconds).

fast.used_for: best bid, best ask, mid, spread

full.used_for: ladder levels and the finest depth bands

sf4.transport: info endpoint POST, polled every 5 s per market (weight 2)

sf3.transport: info endpoint POST, polled every 5 s per market (weight 2)

l2Book.observed_cadence_note: Measured on 2026-11-07 against mainnet: 20-level books pushed about every 5.4 s, 5-level fast books about every 0.54 s. The docs give only the 0.5 minimum and the 'fast' option (5 vs 20 levels); the slower 20-level cadence is an observation, not a documented rule, and the max ages above are set from it.
l2Book.frozen_source: Pushes that arrive with a time that doesn't advance are ignored for freshness, so a frozen source behind a live connection turns stale after max_age_s.
l2Book.stall_rule: If every subscribed market's fast l2Book has been stale for stall_reconnect_s while connected, the collector closes and reopens the connection, which records a gap.
l2Book.subscription_identity_note: WsBook messages carry no nSigFigs field, so two 20-level websocket subscriptions for one coin can't be told apart. The websocket therefore carries only the fast 5-level book and the 20-level full-precision book (told apart by level count: a message with more than 5 levels on a side is the full book; one with fewer than 5 on both sides updates both, since then they're identical; one with exactly 5 on a side updates only the fast book). Aggregated books come from the info endpoint, whose response time field is the source time.

trades.progress_signal: A trade whose time is greater than the trades watermark (the latest trade time seen in the current segment).
trades.reason_when_exceeded: No trade for longer than the max age. A quiet market can't be told apart from a stalled trades feed, so window values are null until a trade arrives.
trades.restart_rule: a coverage gap inside a connection (a malformed or unattributable trades message) restarts progress: the field is warming_up, and every window value is null with the reason, until a valid trade advances the new segment

bbo.reason: The docs: 'Bbo updates that are sent only if the bbo changes on a block'. Silence is normal, so bbo never shows progress; its values are never published as fresh. hl_market reports only its last event time and whether it matches the l2Book top. Best bid and ask come from l2Book.

activeAssetCtx.progress_signal: none usable for freshness: WsActiveAssetCtx carries no source timestamp. A changed context is reported as receipt recency only.
activeAssetCtx.source_time: none: WsActiveAssetCtx carries no time field
activeAssetCtx.watermark: The market's fast l2Book time at the moment the context arrived on the same connection (recorded, not used as a freshness proof).
activeAssetCtx.observed_note: Measured on 2026-11-07: contexts arrived about once a second, and the longest gap between changed contexts was 7.2 s for BTC and HYPE and 17.5 s for the xyz markets.
activeAssetCtx.reason_when_exceeded: no source timestamp, so its source age is unknown; values are null with the receipt age shown

clock_skew.measure: offset_ms = local wall clock at receipt - source time, per l2Book push (median of the last 50).
clock_skew.effect: Reported in hl_status. Source recency is judged through freshness.clock_relationship, so an unknown or exceeded clock bound withholds freshness rather than being ignored.

clearinghouseState.progress_signal: none (a one-shot request when a wallet is opened)
clearinghouseState.rule: judged when the account is served: age = returned time (local wall clock when both the clearinghouseState and frontendOpenOrders answers are in hand, so network delay and the wait for the second answer count) - the answer's time. Fresh only when that age, widened by the clock bound, is within 10 s (freshness.clock_relationship); delayed when older by more than the bound; unverified otherwise, when time is missing, or when the returned time wasn't recorded
clearinghouseState.times_kept: requested, state_received, orders_received and returned (ms, local wall clock)
clearinghouseState.in_the_tab: the tab adds all the time since it sent the request (a monotonic clock) to the age the backend assessed, so delivery to the browser and the time the window stays open count; that over-counts only the backend's own request time, an upper bound. Once age + clock bound passes 10 s, including on arrival, the values are withheld as expired

frontendOpenOrders.source_time: none: the answer is a bare list of orders
frontendOpenOrders.rule: always unverified; values are null with the fetch time in the reason

clock_relationship.decision: Kevin, Nov 8 (GPT review R11 finding 7): a value is fresh only when its feed is still advancing and its source timestamp is recent, judged with a clock relationship whose uncertainty is known; otherwise it is delayed or unverified, never fresh.
clock_relationship.estimate: source_age = local wall clock now - source time
clock_relationship.local_clock_bound: The local wall clock's error bound E: on Linux the kernel's maximum error from adjtimex (maxerror) while the clock is NTP-synchronized; otherwise the plugin setting clock_error_bound_ms; if neither is known, E is unknown.
clock_relationship.source_clock: Hyperliquid's source timestamps are taken as accurate (an assumption; the docs don't state their accuracy). Network delay counts as source age.
clock_relationship.rules: fresh when receipt progress is recent AND source_age + E <= source_max_age AND source_age >= -(E + 1 s); delayed when source_age - E > source_max_age; unverified when E is unknown, the source time is ahead of local time beyond E + 1 s, or source_age is within E of the limit.
clock_relationship.fields_without_source_time: activeAssetCtx has none: it reports receipt recency and an unknown source age, and is never fresh. Another field's timestamp doesn't prove its source recency.

freshness.in_the_tab: the tab ages the snapshot it shows: its age is served.age_s plus all the time since the tab sent the request, so delivery delay and time on screen count. Every status it shows as fresh (the chosen market's fields and every market's Flow Deck trades) is re-judged at that age, as at serving (served_latest): a lapsed field reads stale or delayed with the reason, and every value built on it is withheld in place, null with the reason; a node family LIVE at build time whose delay bound passes its limit reads DELAYED or STALE, with its node values withheld. The page keeps its layout and is never blanked for a delay (Kevin, Nov 8); the delay bar says when the snapshot is past 5 s or a status has lapsed. The empty view is only for having no current snapshot at all
freshness.served_latest: Codex h1 review 1, B1: a tool reading the latest snapshot re-judges each public status fresh at build time at the snapshot's served age: progress_age + age > max_age reads stale, source_age + age + clock bound > source_max_age reads delayed, each with the reason 'by the time this was served'; every value the build gates on that field is withheld as the build withholds it (book_fast: top of book and its price lines; book_full: ladder, exact and observed depth; book_sf4/sf3: approximate and observed depth; trades: flow values, CVD values, large-print count, the Flow Deck card, wallet panels; ctx: context). A snapshot read by ID is historical and stays as of its build time (hl_desk/serving_public.py)

book.best_bid.formula: levels[0][0].px of the fast full-precision l2Book (fast: true, 5 levels)
book.best_bid.completeness_rule: null with reason 'empty bid side' if the side has no levels; null if l2Book isn't fresh

book.best_ask.formula: levels[1][0].px of the fast full-precision l2Book (fast: true, 5 levels)
book.best_ask.completeness_rule: null with reason 'empty ask side' if the side has no levels; null if l2Book isn't fresh

book.mid.completeness_rule: null if either side is null

book.spread.completeness_rule: null if either side is null

book.spread_bps.completeness_rule: null if either side is null

book.level.formula: each returned WsLevel as {px, sz, api_count: n, notional_usd: px*sz}
book.level.units: px USD per coin; sz coin; notional USD
inputs: l2Book full (20 levels, no nSigFigs) for the ladder; nSigFigs=4 and 3 books for depth
book.level.side_convention: bids best first, asks best first
book.level.completeness_rule: only the levels Hyperliquid returned (at most 20 per side per the docs); levels are aggregated, never individual orders; a level whose px or sz is missing, not a number or not positive is never summed, and makes that side's totals (and, at the best level, the mid) unavailable with a reason; n (API count) is a whole number >= 0, otherwise null with a reason, never truncated

book.largest_level.formula: per side, the returned level with the largest aggregate size sz (coin), ties to the level nearer the top of book; reported as the whole level {px, sz, api_count, notional_usd} in levels.largest (hl_market) and drawn as the chart's largest-level price line. Commentary names the largest level only from this field (Codex h1 review 2, B3)
book.largest_level.units: px USD per coin; sz coin; notional USD
book.largest_level.completeness_rule: only among the levels Hyperliquid returned (at most 20 per side); null when that side has no returned level; null with a reason (bid_reason / ask_reason) when any returned level on that side has a missing or invalid px or sz, since it could be the largest (Codex h1 review 3, B1); withheld with the ladder when the 20-level book isn't fresh; an aggregated level, never an individual order

book.depth_band.source: handoff; Kevin's decision 10 (GPT review R11 finding 10)
book.depth_band.outputs: Each band has two separate results: exact (full-precision levels only) and approximate (aggregated buckets). Neither is chosen in place of the other.
book.depth_band.formula: exact: bid depth = sum(px*sz) over the full-precision 20-level book's bid levels with px >= mid*(1-band/100); ask depth = sum(px*sz) over its ask levels with px <= mid*(1+band/100); also in coin (sum sz). approximate: see book.depth_band_approximate.
inputs: mid: the fast book's mid closest to and not after the book's time, within 1.5 s
book.depth_band.window: latest push of the full-precision book
book.depth_band.completeness_rule: exact is available on a side only when that side's deepest returned full-precision level reaches the band edge (bids: lowest px <= edge; asks: highest px >= edge), no returned level on that side is malformed, and the mid is known (a malformed best level makes it unknown). Otherwise exact is null with a reason and 'observed depth within returned levels' is shown with its span; each approximate side names its own resolution (book and bucket width), which can differ between bands and sides

book.depth_imbalance.formula: (bid_depth - ask_depth) / (bid_depth + ask_depth) for one band, computed separately for the exact and the approximate results
book.depth_imbalance.completeness_rule: exact: null unless both sides of the band are exact; approximate: labeled approximate and null unless both sides come from one aggregated book snapshot; null when the sum is zero

book.observed_depth.formula: sum(px*sz) and sum(sz) over all returned levels on one side, with span_pct = |deepest px - mid| / mid * 100
book.observed_depth.completeness_rule: always labeled 'observed depth within returned levels'; never presented as total book depth

book.bbo_consistency.formula: true when the last bbo event's bid and ask prices equal the fast book's best bid and ask; bbo prices themselves are never shown
book.bbo_consistency.window: latest bbo event and latest fast book
book.bbo_consistency.reset_rule: replaced by every bbo event or fast book push
book.bbo_consistency.completeness_rule: null when either input is missing; a consistency signal, not a value

flow.buy_aggressive_notional.formula: sum(px*sz) over trades in the window with side=B
flow.buy_aggressive_notional.window: observed window (max(segment start, W - 15 min), W], half-open, where W is the trades watermark; 15 minutes are retained
flow.buy_aggressive_notional.completeness_rule: the window's actual start, end and whether it covers the requested length are reported; values are null while trades freshness is unverified or warming up

flow.sell_aggressive_notional.formula: sum(px*sz) over trades in the window with side=A

flow.trade_count.formula: number of trades in the execution set within the window

flow.cvd_bucket.formula: per 30 s bucket aligned to source-time multiples of 30 s: buy, sell, delta = buy - sell; cumulative_usd = the running sum of delta from cumulative_from (the start of the snapshot's first complete bucket) through this bucket
flow.cvd_bucket.window: the last 15 minutes of the current segment
flow.cvd_bucket.reset_rule: cumulative delta restarts at every gap
flow.cvd_bucket.completeness_rule: a bucket is complete only if it lies wholly inside the segment and at or before the trades watermark; an incomplete bucket, or any bucket while trades freshness isn't fresh, has null buy, sell, delta and cumulative with a reason; the cumulative sum starts at the snapshot's cumulative origin (cumulative_from: the start of its first complete bucket), not at the first bucket a slice shows; a slice gives that difference as cumulative_base_usd
flow.cvd_bucket.slice: hl_flow returns the last 12 buckets of the snapshot's series without changing their values, and adds slice.cumulative_base_usd = {value, unit: USD}: the cumulative_usd of the last complete bucket before the slice, so cumulative_usd of a shown bucket = cumulative_base_usd + the sum of delta_usd over the complete shown buckets up to it. Its value is 0 only when the series is available and no complete bucket precedes the slice; when the series is withheld (trades not fresh), it is null with that reason, never 0

flow.large_print.formula: a trade with px*sz >= large_print_usd for its market
flow.large_print.completeness_rule: a single public trade can be one of several fills of one taker order; a large print is a trade, not an order; the count is null with a reason while trades freshness isn't fresh (the prints themselves are listed as timed trades)

context.mid.completeness_rule: null unless activeAssetCtx is fresh, or with reason 'midPx absent' when the field is missing

context.funding.formula: WsActiveAssetCtx.ctx.funding, also shown as a percent (funding*100)
context.funding.units: fraction of position notional per funding period
context.funding.period: 1 hour. The funding page says 'The funding rate on Hyperliquid is paid every hour'; the API docs don't state the field's period, so this is a documented-page reading, labeled as such.

context.open_interest.units: coin (inferred from the docs' size convention; the field's unit isn't stated) and USD

context.day_notional_volume.units: USD notional (inferred from the 'Ntl' notation; the field's unit and its exact 24 h window aren't stated)

deck.window.formula: The deck is evaluated at ticks t = k*15 s of source time. A tick is evaluated once the trades watermark has passed t, using the execution set's trades with t - 90 s <= time <= t.
deck.window.reset_rule: each tick is independent (hl_deck: nothing accumulates)
deck.window.completeness_rule: A tick is complete only if t - 90 s is after the segment start. Incomplete ticks are not classified and their numbers are null with reason 'window incomplete'. (plugin rule: hl_deck has no gap handling.)

deck.price.formula: px of the last trade in the window, ordered by time then arrival
deck.price.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete or has no trades

deck.move_bps.formula: (p1 - p0) / p0 * 10000, p0 = px of the first trade and p1 = px of the last trade in the window, ordered by time then arrival
deck.move_bps.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete or has no trades

deck.net_flow.formula: sum(px*sz | side=B) - sum(px*sz | side=A) over the window
deck.net_flow.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete

deck.volume.formula: sum(px*sz | side=B) + sum(px*sz | side=A) over the window
deck.volume.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete

deck.impact.units: bps per $1M: absolute observed trade-price change per $1M of net aggressive flow (unsigned)
deck.impact.completeness_rule: null with reason 'net flow below $100K floor' under the floor (hl_deck shows n/a); null if the window is incomplete
deck.impact.label: absolute observed trade-price change per $1M of net aggressive flow. A descriptive ratio, not an estimate of the price change an additional $1M order would cause.

deck.pressure.source: plugin (Kevin's decision, Nov 8; GPT review R11 finding 8)
deck.pressure.formula: aggressive_buy_notional / aggressive_sell_notional over every valid execution in the window, flips included; available when aggressive_sell_notional >= 25000
deck.pressure.side_convention: above 1 = more aggressive buying than aggressive selling
deck.pressure.completeness_rule: null with reason 'aggressive selling below the $25K floor' under the floor; null if the window is incomplete. The same definition in public and node mode. The data check verifies public trade semantics for every flow number before release.

deck.activity_buckets.source: Handoff 1c position-effect formulas (GPT review R11 finding 8)
deck.activity_buckets.formula: For each participant, from its signed pre-fill position s and fill size q: for a buy, cover_qty = min(q, max(-s, 0)) and new_long_qty = q - cover_qty; for a sell, exit_qty = min(q, max(s, 0)) and new_short_qty = q - exit_qty. Each quantity is converted at that execution's price. The Flow Deck uses only the aggressive participant's effects, so new_long + cover = aggressive buying and new_short + exit = aggressive selling.
inputs: node fills with each participant's starting position (Handoff 1c)
deck.activity_buckets.side_convention: buy side: new-long, cover; sell side: new-short, exit
deck.activity_buckets.completeness_rule: needs node mode (implemented in Handoff 1c Part B). A missing starting position makes the dependent split unavailable, with the unclassified notional shown; it is never treated as zero; a participant's position effect counts only when complete for its side (a buy's cover and new_long, a sell's exit and new_short, none negative, adding up to the fill size; Codex h1 review 4, B2), otherwise its notional is unclassified and the side's buckets are unavailable with the reason, never 0

deck.top_wallet.formula: the taker address with the largest aggressive gross notional (aggressive bought + aggressive sold) in the window; share = that gross / deck.volume
deck.top_wallet.side_convention: both sides combined, taker side only (makers aren't counted, as in hl_deck)
deck.top_wallet.share_label: share of the window's aggressive (taker) notional, both sides
deck.top_wallet.ties: lowest address first (plugin rule; hl_deck keeps the first seen)
deck.top_wallet.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete or deck.volume is 0 (share unavailable, not 0%)

deck.top_wallet_net_aggressive.formula: for the deck.top_wallet address: aggressive bought (sum px*sz of its trades as buyer with side=B) minus aggressive sold (sum px*sz of its trades as seller with side=A) in the window; both parts are reported too
deck.top_wallet_net_aggressive.side_convention: positive = the top wallet's aggressive buying exceeded its aggressive selling
deck.top_wallet_net_aggressive.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete or has no aggressive volume; shown next to the top wallet's share so a wallet that both bought and sold can't read as one-sided

deck.accounts.formula: number of distinct taker addresses in the window
deck.accounts.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete

deck.trade_count.formula: number of trades in the window
deck.trade_count.completeness_rule: null if the window is incomplete

wallets.window.formula: requested window (W - N min, W], half-open, where W is the trades watermark and N is 1, 5 or 15; actual window (max(W - N min, segment start), W]
wallets.window.completeness_rule: complete only if the actual start equals the requested start; the actual start, end and completeness are always shown; null while trades freshness is unverified
wallets.window.window: 1, 5 or 15 minutes ending at the trades watermark, never reaching before the current segment's start

wallets.unique_execution_notional.formula: sum(px*sz) over the window's executions, each counted once
wallets.unique_execution_notional.side_convention: both sides (equals total bought and total sold)

wallets.executions.formula: number of executions in the window (window total) or involving the wallet (per wallet; a self-trade counts once)

wallets.bought.formula: sum(px*sz) over executions in the window where the wallet is users[0] (buyer), maker or taker

wallets.sold.formula: sum(px*sz) over executions in the window where the wallet is users[1] (seller), maker or taker
wallets.sold.completeness_rule: as wallets.window; a self-trade (buyer = seller) counts once to bought and once to sold

wallets.aggressive_bought.formula: sum(px*sz) over the wallet's bought executions with side=B

wallets.aggressive_sold.formula: sum(px*sz) over the wallet's sold executions with side=A

wallets.participation.completeness_rule: participation, never market volume: a trade counts to two wallets

wallets.net_bought.completeness_rule: net bought notional, not a position change or PnL

wallets.buy_share.formula: wallet bought / sum of bought over every buyer in the market and window (including wallets not shown)
wallets.buy_share.completeness_rule: null with reason 'no buying in window' when the total is 0 (unavailable, not 0%)

wallets.sell_share.formula: wallet sold / sum of sold over every seller in the market and window
wallets.sell_share.completeness_rule: null with reason 'no selling in window' when the total is 0

wallets.ranked_list.formula: buyers ranked by bought desc, sellers by sold desc, ties by address ascending; list the shortest ranked prefix whose cumulative share reaches target_share_pct, or cap wallets, whichever comes first
wallets.ranked_list.completeness_rule: always report the share reached and whether the target or the cap stopped the list, e.g. 'Top 50 make up 25% of buying; the 50% target isn't reached.'

chart.candle.formula: per 15 s interval aligned to source-time multiples of 15 s: open = px of the first trade, high = max px, low = min px, close = px of the last trade (ordered by time then arrival), volume_usd = sum(px*sz) of its trades, summed exactly and rounded to cents once
chart.candle.window: aligned 15 s candles from the candle boundary at or before (trades watermark - 15 minutes) to the watermark, within the current coverage segment; trades are retained for 16 minutes, so the oldest candle holds every trade of its interval
chart.candle.reset_rule: restarts at every gap (candles come from the current segment only)
chart.candle.completeness_rule: complete is false for a candle that starts at or before the segment start or ends after the trades watermark; the rolling 15-minute cutoff never truncates a candle, because the window starts on a candle boundary and includes a trade exactly at that boundary; candles are timed summaries of public trades, drawn as a chart

chart.price_line.formula: horizontal lines at: best bid and best ask (fast book), mark and oracle (activeAssetCtx), and the largest-size returned level on each side of the 20-level book (an aggregated level, labeled with its size and API count)
chart.price_line.completeness_rule: a line is drawn only when its value is available (fresh); missing lines are simply absent; the largest-level lines are drawn from book.largest_level, so a side whose largest isn't established has no line, listed in price_lines_withheld with the reason

deck.pressure_legacy_hl_deck.formula: (new_long + cover) / (new_short + exit) with hl_deck's dir filter, which leaves out flips (Long > Short, Short > Long)
deck.pressure_legacy_hl_deck.completeness_rule: not computed in this version. If ever shown, only as a separately named legacy comparison; never used by the classifier, and agreement with it is not evidence that leaving out flips is correct.

book.depth_band_approximate.source: plugin; Kevin's decision 10 (GPT review R11 finding 10)
book.depth_band_approximate.formula: For each band and side, the finest aggregated book (nSigFigs=4, then nSigFigs=3) whose returned buckets reach the band edge: approx_usd = sum(px*sz) over buckets whose representative (returned) price is inside the band. range_usd = [approx_usd - notional of the outermost bucket counted, approx_usd + notional of the nearest bucket left out], because Hyperliquid doesn't document bucket alignment, so the bucket at the edge may be partly in or out.
book.depth_band_approximate.units: USD notional (an estimate: representative price times aggregate size)
book.depth_band_approximate.window: latest poll of the aggregated book
book.depth_band_approximate.completeness_rule: labeled approximate, with its aggregation and bucket width; unavailable with the books tried and their reasons when no fresh aggregated book reaches the edge, a level on that side is malformed, or the mid is unknown. Never shown as exact.

wallet.current_account_value.window: the account state at the answer's own time (not part of any snapshot)
wallet.current_account_value.reset_rule: fetched again each time a wallet is opened
wallet.current_account_value.completeness_rule: null with a reason unless the answer's freshness (freshness.fields.clearinghouseState) is fresh; a missing field is null with a reason, and a missing assetPositions makes the positions unknown, not empty

wallet.current_total_position_notional.window: the account state at the answer's own time (not part of any snapshot)
wallet.current_total_position_notional.reset_rule: fetched again each time a wallet is opened
wallet.current_total_position_notional.completeness_rule: null with a reason unless the answer's freshness (freshness.fields.clearinghouseState) is fresh; a missing field is null with a reason, and a missing assetPositions makes the positions unknown, not empty

wallet.current_margin_used.window: the account state at the answer's own time (not part of any snapshot)
wallet.current_margin_used.reset_rule: fetched again each time a wallet is opened
wallet.current_margin_used.completeness_rule: null with a reason unless the answer's freshness (freshness.fields.clearinghouseState) is fresh; a missing field is null with a reason, and a missing assetPositions makes the positions unknown, not empty

wallet.current_position.formula: per entry of assetPositions[].position on the market's dex: size_coin = szi (signed: positive long, negative short), entry_px = entryPx, position_value_usd = positionValue, unrealized_pnl_usd = unrealizedPnl, margin_used_usd = marginUsed, liquidation_px = liquidationPx (null with a reason when Hyperliquid gives none), leverage = leverage.value with leverage.type
wallet.current_position.window: the account state at the answer's own time (not part of any snapshot)
wallet.current_position.reset_rule: fetched again each time a wallet is opened
wallet.current_position.completeness_rule: null with a reason unless the answer's freshness (freshness.fields.clearinghouseState) is fresh; a missing field is null with a reason, and a missing assetPositions makes the positions unknown, not empty

wallet.current_open_orders.formula: the frontendOpenOrders list for the user and the market's dex
wallet.current_open_orders.reset_rule: fetched again each time a wallet is opened
wallet.current_open_orders.completeness_rule: always unverified and null with a reason: the answer carries no response timestamp, so whether the set is current can't be established (freshness.fields.frontendOpenOrders); an order's placement time doesn't establish it

trades.validity.formula: a trade is valid when px > 0, sz > 0, integer time and tid, side in {B, A}, users = two 0x addresses (40 hex), and coin equal to the subscription's coin
trades.validity.side_convention: side is the aggressor: B = buyer took, A = seller took
trades.validity.completeness_rule: an invalid trade in a live message ends the coverage segment (a gap with the missing fields as its reason) and a new segment starts after the latest time in that message; the message's valid trades are on the tape, uncounted; nothing is filled in (no default side, address or tid)
trades.validity.routing: a trades message is routed by its records' coins, never by the first record alone. Records naming no coin or another coin are invalid records of the subscribed coin the message names. A message naming no subscribed coin, with a record lacking its coin, can't be attributed, so it ends every subscribed market's trade coverage as a gap

deck.late_trades.formula: a trade whose time is at or before the last evaluated tick re-evaluates, from the earliest tick whose 90 s window contains it, every retained tick (the last 8), starting from the latch state saved before that tick: window numbers, live classification, pending/confirmed latch and the regime-change events those ticks produced are re-derived from the execution set. A regime change the re-evaluation no longer supports is withdrawn with a 'regime_change_withdrawn' event, and the card carries 'revised' with the late-trade count and the ticks re-evaluated
deck.late_trades.window: the retained ticks (about 2 minutes); a trade later than that falls outside every displayed card's window and leaves older latch steps as evaluated
deck.late_trades.reset_rule: cleared at every gap with the rest of the deck
deck.late_trades.completeness_rule: the displayed card's numbers always equal the execution set's totals for its window; delivering trades late or in order ends in the same card, latch and regime changes

node.family_state.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.family_state.formula: per family (book, triggers, depth, bands, flow): INVALID if not recovered; REPLAY for a valid replay family; UNKNOWN when client wall - pub_ms < -1000 ms; STALE when no freshness-advancing watermark since the family became valid; otherwise from the node feed's delay (Kevin, Nov 8): delay(t) = wall at the market's latest timed watermark's receipt - its block_time_ms + monotonic time since receipt, averaged exactly over the last 5000 ms (or since the first watermark) = delay_ms; STALE when delay_ms > 30000; BEHIND (shown as DELAYED) when delay_ms > 10000; else LIVE. Heartbeats never count, so a silent feed's delay keeps growing
node.family_state.reset_rule: per producer session and replay session
node.family_state.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.level_total_sz.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.level_total_sz.formula: sum of resting executable order sizes at the price level
node.level_total_sz.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.level_orders.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.level_orders.formula: count of resting executable orders at the level
node.level_orders.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.largest_order_size_at_level.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.largest_order_size_at_level.formula: size of the largest single resting order at the level; its time is that same order's (tie: earliest time, then lowest oid). Label: 'largest order size at this level'
node.largest_order_size_at_level.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.oldest_resting_order_at_level.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.oldest_resting_order_at_level.formula: earliest time_ms of any resting order at the level, a separate statistic. Label: 'oldest resting order at this level'
node.oldest_resting_order_at_level.units: ms since epoch (shown as an age)
node.oldest_resting_order_at_level.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.level_change_10s.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.level_change_10s.formula: per level over the last 10 s of block time: added (op add), absorbed (the part of a decrease covered by maker_filled), pulled (a removal with status canceled and maker_filled 0), unknown (anything else). Never 'moved'
node.level_change_10s.reset_rule: restarts at every gap (the change history never bridges one)
node.level_change_10s.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.stops_band.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.stops_band.formula: waiting stop/take-profit orders grouped by trigger price into [k*width, (k+1)*width) per kind and side, within 2% of the book mid: orders, stated size (sum of sizes of orders with a size), whole-position orders (size unknown, counted), the largest order and its share of the stated size; dominated when one order is more than 50% of it. Everything outside the range is counted below/above (or under no reference price); stated size is a lower bound (sz_lower_bound, with sz_note) when the band holds whole-position TP/SL orders (unknown_size_orders, no stated size), and unknown (sz null with sz_reason) when every order in it is one, never 0 (Node Project review B2, Nov 9). The set is checked against the venue only when the engine restarts (venue_check)
node.stops_band.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in; every waiting trigger accounted for; trailing stops left out by the engine and counted

node.wall.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.wall.formula: orders within 2% of the mid at least 5x the median order notional there; the 5 largest per side; outcome labelled from lifecycle records only
node.wall.window: observed since the book became valid
node.wall.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.heatmap_sample.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.heatmap_sample.formula: every 5 s of block time: per price bin (the market's band width) within 2% of the mid, resting bid and ask notional
node.heatmap_sample.reset_rule: restarts at every gap; partial until it covers 15 minutes
node.heatmap_sample.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in

node.thinning_band.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.thinning_band.formula: per 0.5% band out to 10% from the mid, bids below and asks above: depth_usd = sum(px*sz) of resting orders in the band; usd_per_1_price = depth_usd / (mid * 0.005); orders; the largest single order and its share (dominated over 50%); sharpest drop = the largest ratio usd_per_1_price[k] / usd_per_1_price[k+1] moving away from the price, with its band and distance (an empty next band is called empty)
node.thinning_band.completeness_rule: null with the family's state and reason unless the family is valid; LIVE only after a watermark the client has applied every message before; heartbeats never count; INVALID after a gap, new producer session, dropped connection or incomplete snapshot until the family's own snapshot is swapped in; note: What's resting right now. Orders can be added or pulled at any moment; this isn't a forecast.

node.activity_buckets.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.activity_buckets.formula: over the executions of the window, counted once by (market, tid): aggressive buying = the taker's new_long and cover where the taker bought; aggressive selling = the taker's new_short and exit where it sold; each at the execution's price (bucket size x px). Percentages: buying buckets / aggressive buy notional, selling buckets / aggressive sell notional, over the same executions. Effects from each participant's signed start position s and fill size q: buy cover = min(q, max(-s,0)), new_long = q - cover; sell exit = min(q, max(s,0)), new_short = q - exit
node.activity_buckets.units: USD; % of the side's aggressive notional
node.activity_buckets.window: the card's 90 s window or the burst's 60 s window, in node fills
node.activity_buckets.reset_rule: restarts after the first watermark following a gap, new session, replay session change or fills_known false
node.activity_buckets.completeness_rule: unavailable with a reason and the unclassified notional when any taker effect, role or identity is missing; unavailable when node fills don't cover the window; never scaled to 100%; a participant's position effect counts only when complete for its side (a buy's cover and new_long, a sell's exit and new_short, none negative, adding up to the fill size; Codex h1 review 4, B2), otherwise its notional is unclassified and the side's buckets are unavailable with the reason, never 0

node.wallet_split.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.wallet_split.formula: per wallet: full split = its own participant effects over all its fills (maker and taker), new_long and cover over its total bought notional, new_short and exit over its total sold notional; aggressive split = its taker fills only over its aggressive bought / sold notional
node.wallet_split.window: the wallets panel's window, in node fills
node.wallet_split.completeness_rule: a zero denominator gives an unavailable percentage; a missing effect, role or side makes the split unavailable with the unclassified notional

node.liquidation.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.liquidation.formula: one per (liquidated trader, liquidated participant's oid), its fills summed; long when the liquidated participant sold with exit > 0, short when it bought with cover > 0
node.liquidation.completeness_rule: position unknown (with a reason) when the effect is missing

node.liquidation_burst.source: node feed (l4-livefeed protocol v2, PROTOCOL.md revision 2.2)
node.liquidation_burst.formula: liquidations (counted once each) within 60 s of block time >= liq_burst_count (default 2) or their notional >= liq_burst_usd (default 1,000,000); rearms when the window falls below both; evaluated at each node executions message and each watermark at its own block time t, over (t - 60 s, t] (Codex h1 review 4, B1): it fires once when the window reaches a threshold and re-arms when the window falls below both, a quiet market's at its watermarks

regimes.order: first match wins, in this order

rules.when: the complete window has no trades
volume < 150000 and |move_bps| >= 2.0; UP if move_bps > 0 else DOWN
|move_bps| >= 5.0 and |net_flow| >= 40000 and (move_bps > 0) != (net_flow > 0); OFFERS if move_bps > 0 else BIDS
impact is not null (|net_flow| >= 100000) and impact >= 20.0 and |move_bps| >= 1.0; UP if move_bps > 0 else DOWN
impact is not null and impact <= 2.0
|move_bps| >= 3.0 and PRESSURE (aggressive buy / aggressive sell notional) is available (selling >= $25K) and >= 1.15 and move_bps > 0
|move_bps| >= 3.0 and PRESSURE is available (selling >= $25K) and <= 0.87 and move_bps < 0
nothing above matched (including a >= 3 bps move whose PRESSURE is unavailable or between 0.87 and 1.15)

regimes.display_rule_sparse: If the window has between 1 and 4 trades and its live classification isn't VACUUM-UP or VACUUM-DOWN, the live classification is flagged sparse with the SPARSE explanation. The flag never enters the latch or the events list (hl_deck 450-453).
regimes.latch: A classification different from the confirmed regime must repeat on 2 consecutive complete ticks to become the confirmed regime; a different classification restarts the count at 1; a return to the confirmed regime clears the pending count. Until the first confirmation the live classification is shown as unconfirmed. Confirmation sets 'since' to that tick's time (hl_deck 423-448).
regimes.events: A confirmed change creates an event 'PREV -> NEW (held Ns)' when a previous confirmed regime existed; held = this tick's time - the previous regime's since (hl_deck 439-441).
regimes.gap_rule: plugin rule: at a gap the confirmed regime ends, an event 'PREV -> (gap)' records how long it held up to the segment's last complete tick, and the latch clears. No regime, held time or event spans a gap.
regimes.held: card held = latest complete tick time - since, in source time
regimes.decisions: Kevin, Nov 8, accepting GPT review R11 findings 8 and 9: PRESSURE is aggressive buy notional over aggressive sell notional (flips included, $25K selling floor) in both modes, so TRENDING can fire on public data and the UNRESOLVED state is removed; the explanations below replace hl_deck's GUIDE wording and claim no cause the numbers can't show; the confirmed regime, the live classification and any pending change are shown separately.
regimes.display: Each card reports three things separately, with their times: confirmed_regime (the latched regime, since and held), live_classification (what this tick's window numbers classify as, with its explanation) and pending (a different classification waiting for its second consecutive tick). The confirmed label is never presented as describing different current numbers.

ABSORBING.text: Small observed trade-price change relative to net aggressive notional. Absorption is a hypothesis; this calculation does not identify an absorber or its remaining size.

VACUUM-UP.text: Price moved with low total traded notional or a high price-change/net-flow ratio, as indicated by the branch tag. This calculation does not measure resting-book depth or predict a reversal.

VACUUM-DOWN.text: Price moved with low total traded notional or a high price-change/net-flow ratio, as indicated by the branch tag. This calculation does not measure resting-book depth or predict a reversal.

PULLED-OFFERS.text: Observed trade prices rose while net aggressive flow was selling. The cause is undetermined; this classification does not establish offer cancellations.

PULLED-BIDS.text: Observed trade prices fell while net aggressive flow was buying. The cause is undetermined; this classification does not establish bid cancellations.

TRENDING-UP.text: The window meets the stated upward price-move and buy/sell-ratio thresholds. This describes the observed window and does not establish that the move will continue or end at a particular ratio.

TRENDING-DOWN.text: The window meets the stated downward price-move and buy/sell-ratio thresholds. This describes the observed window and does not establish that the move will continue or end at a particular ratio.

BALANCED.text: None of the earlier classifier conditions matched. This is not a measurement of trader commitment or expected profitability.

THIN.text: Traded notional and observed trade-price movement are below this classifier's stated thresholds. Resting-book depth is not measured by this label.

SPARSE.text: Fewer than five executions support this window. Displayed ratios are based on very few observations.

QUIET.text: No qualifying executions occurred in the complete observed window. This is distinct from an unavailable or unverified feed.

regimes.meanings_source: GPT review R11 finding 9's replacement text, adopted by Kevin on Nov 8. Regimes are heuristic classifications of the stated execution-window measurements; their labels do not establish a cause, a participant's intent or remaining size, or a profitable trading opportunity. hl_deck's original GUIDE wording is no longer shown.

burst.formula: For each side, the aggressive notional of trades with time in (W - 60 s, W], where W is the trades watermark after each trades message: sum(px*sz | side=B) for buying, sum(px*sz | side=A) for selling.
burst.side_convention: buying = side B trades; selling = side A trades
burst.window: 60 s trailing, evaluated at each new trades watermark
burst.reset_rule: After a side fires it is disarmed. It re-arms when that side's 60 s sum, evaluated just before the trades of a new message are added (the minimum since the last evaluation, because the sum only falls between messages), is below the threshold; a gap also re-arms it and starts a new segment. One burst episode fires once.
burst.completeness_rule: Evaluated only when W - 60 s is at or after the segment start, so a burst never spans a gap.
burst.wallets: The aggressive participants (takers) of the burst's own executions, each with its aggressive notional on that side, ranked against the burst's total with the wallets.ranked_list rules (target 50%, cap 50, ties by address). Shares use the burst total as the denominator.
burst.config: public mode: per-market threshold in plugin settings burst_min_usd (BTC default $10M from the handoff; other defaults are plugin choices); node mode: automatic per market from the burst calibration 2026-11-08.1 (dated 2026-11-08, measured 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-08 UTC exclusive, i.e. Nov 3 to 7; target 10 a day; BTC $30M, 10.6 a day; HYPE $5M, 14.6 a day; xyz:SP500 $5M, 7.2 a day; xyz:XYZ100 $5M, 11.0 a day), or manual per market in node_burst_min_usd

node_mode.source: Kevin, Nov 8: burst calibration option A (analysis PLAN.md 'The burst rule', 'Validation', 'The reference for ranks', 'The default for the first release')
node_mode.applies: node mode only (a node feed is configured): bursts come from node fills and public-trades bursts aren't shown; public mode keeps alerts.burst above and burst_min_usd
node_mode.rule: For each side, the taker notional (px*sz) of the market's node executions in (W - 60 s, W], evaluated once per node block (W = the block time of each node executions message). A disarmed side re-arms when its sum before this block's executions are added is below the threshold; then, if armed and the sum has reached the threshold, it fires once and disarms. A gap (a sequence gap, a new producer or replay session) re-arms both sides and starts a new segment at the node fills' next window start; no burst spans a gap.
node_mode.incomplete_windows: A window that starts before the segment start, or that contains a rejected or unreadable record, keeps its executions but never fires, re-arms or disarms.
node_mode.rejected_records: An execution that can't be read (tid, price, size or time); complete false or conflict; not exactly one taker and one maker, one buyer and one seller, each with an address; a fill time other than the block time; an identity already seen in an earlier block; a block whose fills weren't read (fills_known false); a block time running backwards. Rejected executions are never counted.
node_mode.threshold: Per market: automatic, from the dated, versioned calibration hl_desk/node/calibration/burst-calibration-2026-11-08.json (target 10 bursts a covered day, measured Nov 3 to 7 on node fills: the grid threshold whose achieved rate is nearest the target), labelled 'automatic: about 10 a day, measured Nov 3 to 7', or with the achieved rate when no threshold is within 25% of the target; or manual, from the setting node_burst_min_usd (a market listed with a number). Removing the market from node_burst_min_usd, or setting it to "auto", restores the automatic threshold. Without either, node bursts are unavailable for that market, with the reason.
node_mode.rank: Each node burst's rank against the calibration's reference (every eligible 60 s sum of the same market and side, sampled every 15 s, Nov 3 to 7): count(reference sums >= burst sum) / reference count, ties counted as at or above, shown as 'a top x% minute, Nov 3 to 7'. When the reference file isn't loaded the rank is unavailable, never estimated.
node_mode.event: type burst, stream 'node fills', with side, at_ms, block, the window, aggressive_notional_usd, threshold {usd, source, label, version, achieved_per_day, ...}, rank {upper_tail, top_pct, at_or_above, reference_count, label} or {available false, reason}, wallets (the aggressive takers, wallets.ranked_list rules) and node_activity (the side's buckets from exactly these executions)

calibration.refresh: a newer calibration ships as a new dated version. Thresholds are read when the collector starts, so a change (a new version or a manual threshold) takes effect at a restart, which is a gap: a new segment with its 60 s warm-up, and no window from before it. As after any gap, a window whose sum is at or above the new threshold then fires once at its first complete evaluation

regime_change.reset_rule: events are kept newest first, the last 50 per market
regime_change.completeness_rule: only complete ticks change the latch

items: BUYER GONE / SELLER GONE / BUYER BACK / SELLER BACK / FLIPPED (portable to public data, not in v1 scope)
not_ported.reason: Handoff 1 step 5a asks for regime events and burst alerts. hl_deck's other alerts are recorded here and left for a later version.
